title: ewf-universal
label: Turbulence

won.source: WrestleFest 2003, the final of the fed’s own Universal Championship tournament: “The winner of this match will be crowned the very first EWF Universal Champion!”

how: won the Universal Championship Tournament Final at WrestleFest 2003, busting "The Turnbuckle" Jay Krazy open on the Spanish announce table and finishing him with a chair and a metal baseball bat after Baz overruled a disqualification and ordered the match to continue as No Disqualification
note: Still champion on the fed’s own champions page at its last capture, 19 April 2003.

title: ewf-international
label: Super Rob

won.source: The fed’s own champions page, captured 19 April 2003, names him International Champion; nothing records the change.

note: How the belt passed from The Overweighter is not in the surviving record — no served show or news post names a change. Super Rob never appears in either surviving show script.

title: ewf-international
label: The Overweighter

won.source: WrestleFest 2003: “Ladies and gentlemen here is your winner and new International Champion… The Overweighter!”

how: won the belt at WrestleFest 2003 from Darren "Big 9" Sin, with a Coke Slam and The Last Meal

title: ewf-international-tag-team
label: Blood Man & J

won.source: WrestleFest 2003: a tag team elimination match, eliminating John Dumas (pinned after a chair shot unseen by the referee) and Chaos (pinned by Blood Man's Bleeding Blood and J's own J Splash). The fed’s own champions page, captured 19 April 2003, still names them “Elite Wrestling Federation International Tag Team Champions / Blood Man & J”.

how: won the vacant Tag Team Championship at WrestleFest 2003 by eliminating John Dumas and Chaos in a tag team elimination match
note: WrestleFest's own commentary and ring announcement call this simply the “EWF Tag team championship,” without “International”; the champions page, captured six weeks later, names it the “International Tag Team” champions. Both are held as the same belt.
